title: A zero error shifts the line
caption: Hooke's law predicts an extension through the origin (lower line). A line crossing the extension axis at 3 mm (upper line) points to a constant systematic offset, a zero error such as measuring the length from the wrong point. The two lines are parallel, so the gradient (the stiffness) is unaffected. The gradient used here, 2 mm per N, is only illustrative.
alt: Two parallel straight lines of extension against load: one through the origin and one crossing the extension axis at 3 millimetres.
description: Horizontal axis: the load in newtons; vertical axis: the measured extension in millimetres.
The expected line e = kF passes through the origin.
The measured line crosses the extension axis at 3 mm: every reading is 3 mm too large, a constant (systematic) offset.
The two lines have the same gradient, so a fit to the slope still gives the right stiffness, while the intercept reveals the error.
